- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in subsequent periods.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is > 65.0, forecast should be ≥ 65.5; if < 63.0, forecast should be ≤ 62.5.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- In 30-day horizon, model tends to ignore sentiment volatility; if sentiment swings >2 in 3 days, reduce forecast variance by 10–15% to reflect uncertainty.
